newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria shares slip, CA under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Austria shares slip, CA under pressure.

text.p: Austrian shares ended only moderately weaker on Thursday despite a 10 percent slump in the price of Creditanstalt preferred as investors bailed out following the bank's sale to Bank Austria.

The ATX index of 21 blue-chip shares closed 1.42 points, or 0.12 percent, down at 1,167.94. January ATX futures, which go off the board on Friday, advanced 1.6 points to 1,166.8 and traders were unanimous in forecasting an expiry near 1,160.
Overall 14 ATX shares closed down and seven up.
Preferred shares in Creditanstalt-Bankverein were by far the biggest decliner on unusually high turnover. The stock finished 43.05 schillings, or 9.34 percent, down at 417.95.
Bank Austria has acquired the state's 70 percent of ordinary Creditanstalt shares and offered to buy out small investors but it has given no clues about its plans for holders of preferred shares.
"Turnover is amazing. The stock is in a downward spiral," a trader said.
Volume was 231,763 lots, well above average daily turnover of nearer 20,000.
Traders said the preference shares could fall as low as 400 before rebounding. Creditanstalt ordinary shares closed five schillings down at 714.
Luxury hosiery maker Wolford was the leading gainer, boosted by one big buy order. Its shares jumped 78 schillings, or 6.14 percent, to 1,348.
Market participants also pinpointed investor demand for oil and chemicals group OMV, which climbed 29 schillings to 1,327.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index slipped 1.9 points, or 0.43 percent, to 436.19. -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
